note: Config for scripts/voice_batch.py. Run it from <project>/ with --dry-run first, then, after the owner's yes for the batch and its cap, with --merge-manifest so each finished take lands in voices.json. Paths are relative to <project>/. Fill in the top-level placeholders (stt_quick, stt_words and aligner_label, which --no-stt does not read) and those of the voices you run; delete the voices and the generate cap keys you do not use (unpaid local voices read no caps). The scratch voice uses the macOS say command; on Linux or Windows, replace its command with "espeak-ng -v {voice} -w {out} -f {text_file}", its command_ext with "wav" and its model with "espeak-ng" (references/example-speech-providers.md). max_requests applies to each generation call, and each regeneration round is a new call, so one voice can make up to (1 + --max-regens) x max_requests attempts; the USD caps bound the whole batch through the ledger. The generate block applies to every API voice and to any command voice marked "paid": true; tts_generate.py refuses a live paid run without a ledger, an explicit estimate and a cap. Working transcriber commands: references/example-local-tools.md. An openai-speech voice may add instructions_file, a path relative to the project.

generate.est_usd_per_request: <list-price estimate per request, from the vendor's price page on the day>

voices.label: Narrator
voices.design_prompt: <the voice's design prompt, for a designed voice; delete the key otherwise>
